title: Legacy execution import snapshot
description: The full-fidelity import record of ONE pre-cutover execution-runs.json entry, written by the Phase-8 state migrator (docs/operations/migration/MIGRATOR-DESIGN.md §5). A small typed header correlates the import to its workflow instance and operation; the `legacy` member preserves the VERBATIM legacy entry — every timestamp, attempt count, review link, cost/governance field, failure reason, and pre-exec baseline exactly as persisted. This kind exists because ExecutionProvenance requires compiled-mode/prompt-catalog digests that never existed for legacy runs: fabricating them would violate the no-fabricated-identity rule, so legacy history gets its own dedicated import kind instead of a fake provenance record. The workflow's correlated OperationExecutionRecord pins this document by digest (provenance_digest = sha256 of these exact bytes).

operation.description: The registered operation the legacy entry maps onto (generator -> execution-run, retry -> execution-retry, fixup -> execution-fixup, followup -> execution-followup).

execution_id.description: The correlated execution id: the entry's op_execution_id when the cutover already assigned one, else exec-legacy-<legacy execution_id>.

workflow_instance_id.description: The instance_id of the workflow whose operations[] correlates this import.

imported_at.description: Deterministic import instant: the legacy entry's own last-write time (updated_at, else finished_at, else queued_at) — never wall clock, so repeated staging is byte-identical.

legacy.description: The verbatim legacy execution-runs.json entry, byte-preserved. Never normalized, trimmed, or re-keyed.
